record.paper_title: Three open problems in function theoretic operator theory
record.context_brief: universal adjoints of affine composition operators
record.original_question: Let C_+ be the right half-plane, let H^2(C_+) be the Hardy space on C_+, and let phi : C_+ -> C_+ be an affine self-map. Let C_phi be the composition operator on H^2(C_+) and C_phi^* its adjoint. Is C_phi^* - lambda I universal on H^2(C_+) for some complex scalar lambda if and only if phi is elliptic and not an automorphism? Here universal means that every bounded operator on the ambient separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space is similar, up to a nonzero scalar multiple, to the restriction of the universal operator to some invariant subspace.

evidence.quote: Question 5.20. If phi : C+ -> C+ is an affine map

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{C}_+ = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : \operatorname{Re} z > 0\}$ denote the right half-plane, and let $H^2(\mathbb{C}_+)$ be the Hardy space on $\mathbb{C}_+$, consisting of analytic functions $f : \mathbb{C}_+ \to \mathbb{C}$ with
$$\|f\|^2 := \sup_{x>0} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} |f(x+iy)|^2\, dy < \infty.$$
For an analytic self-map $\varphi : \mathbb{C}_+ \to \mathbb{C}_+$ for which the composition operator $C_\varphi f := f \circ \varphi$ is bounded on $H^2(\mathbb{C}_+)$, write $C_\varphi^*$ for its Hilbert space adjoint.

A bounded operator $U$ on a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ is called universal if, for every bounded linear operator $T$ on $\mathcal{H}$, there exist a nonzero scalar $\mu \in \mathbb{C}$ and a closed $U$-invariant subspace $\mathcal{M} \subset \mathcal{H}$ such that $\mu T$ is similar to the restriction $U|_{\mathcal{M}}$.

An affine self-map of $\mathbb{C}_+$ is a map of the form $\varphi(z) = az + b$ with $a > 0$ and $\operatorname{Re} b \ge 0$. Such a $\varphi$ is called elliptic when it has a fixed point in $\mathbb{C}_+$, and it is an automorphism of $\mathbb{C}_+$ precisely when $b \in i\mathbb{R}$ (so $\varphi$ is a translation when $a=1$).

Problem: Prove or disprove that, for every affine self-map $\varphi$ of $\mathbb{C}_+$ such that $C_\varphi$ is bounded on $H^2(\mathbb{C}_+)$, the operator $C_\varphi^* - \lambda I$ is universal on $H^2(\mathbb{C}_+)$ for some $\lambda \in \mathbb{C}$ if and only if $\varphi$ is elliptic and not an automorphism of $\mathbb{C}_+$.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (Cowen–Gallardo-Gutiérrez and subsequent papers on universal composition operators, including extensions to weighted Dirichlet spaces) characterizes certain linear fractional symbols whose composition operators or their adjoints have universal translates, but the full affine-symbol characterization on H^2 of the half-plane is posed as an open question and does not appear to be resolved in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Universal composition operators
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizes linear fractional composition operators with universal translates on H^2 of the disk and half-plane; identifies new affine examples.
status_evidence.claim: Partial characterizations exist but the affine-symbol case on H^2(C_+) is not fully settled.

status_evidence.title: Universal composition operators on weighted Dirichlet spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizes composition operators and their adjoints induced by affine self-maps of the upper half-plane with universal translates on weighted Dirichlet spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Related cases are studied; the H^2(C_+) affine version remains stated as a question.
